title: 215-16 Northern Boulevard: street-wall location, the 23-433 setback trigger at or below the base height, and R6B side yards (ZR 23-431, 35-631; 23-432/23-433, 35-632; 23-335, 34-232)

question.text: For a building on lot 70 (R6B with a C2-2 overlay, corner of Northern Boulevard and 215 Place): (Q1) where must the street wall sit along each frontage, and does the C2-2 overlay change the rule for a residential-only building and for a mixed building? (Q2) does ZR 23-433 require any setback for a building at or below the maximum base height (the benchmark three-storey 30 ft option), and on what condition? (Q3) is a side yard required, optional or prohibited in R6B, and under which section?
question.property: 215-16 Northern Boulevard, Queens (borough 4, block 7334, lot 70; BBL 4073340070; R6B with a C2-2 overlay; corner of Northern Boulevard and 215 Place)

exceptions_considered: 35-631(a) line-up applies only to Commercial Districts with an R8 through R12 equivalent in the Manhattan Core; this site is R6B in Queens, so (a) does not apply and (b) governs.

35-631(b) and 23-431 each contain a closing clause: where the block has a #prevailing street wall frontage# further from the street line than the paragraph's own provisions, the line-up rules of 23-431(a) may be applied. Whether such a prevailing frontage exists on either frontage is an unresearched adjacency fact (condition).

35-631(c) modifications for large zoning lots ('for #street walls# on #buildings# on a #zoning lot# that has a #lot area# of at least 40,000 square feet or occupies an entire #block#, at least 70 percent of the #aggregate width of street walls# shall be located within 15 feet of the #street line#') are inapplicable: lot 70's recorded area is about 10,075 sq ft (NB-04), well under 40,000 sq ft, and it does not occupy the whole block.

35-631(d) articulation allowances apply in all districts and on all frontages (projections/recesses up to 12 inches generally; and up to 50 percent of the aggregate street-wall width may recess or project up to 3 feet), permitting facade articulation beyond the (b) location without changing the governing rule; no projection may extend beyond the street line except where the Administrative Code permits.
35-632(b) eligible-site height increases apply to R6 through R12 WITHOUT a letter suffix; R6B has a letter suffix, so (b) does not apply. 35-632(c) towers apply to R9 through R12; not R6B.

23-335(a) (two 5 ft side yards) applies only to single- or two-family detached residences; a multi-family or mixed building falls under 23-335(b) (no side yard required). In the overlay 34-232 removes the side-yard requirement for ANY residential building.
The wide/narrow classification's alternate-width provisions noted in the repository (12-10 'street, wide' amended 2026-03-26 for C5-3/C6-4/C6-6) do not apply to an R6B/C2-2 site.
FAR, lot coverage, the rear yard (NB-03), lot dimensions (NB-04), special-density or MIH overlays, parking, use, and obstructions are separate questions and are not resolved here.

ZR 23-433(a) to (d) may reduce or adjust the setback depths where a setback is triggered above the maximum base height: a one-foot-for-one-foot reduction with a seven-foot floor, and the setback is optional for a building wall beyond 50 feet of a street line or oriented so a perpendicular meets a street line at 65 degrees or less (23-433(c)). These modify only a setback that is triggered; the benchmark 30-foot option triggers none.
meaning_and_applicability.reading: A labelled DRAFT reading, not a DOB determination. Q1 (street wall). ZR 23-431(a) is the residence-district rule for R6B: a line-up with eligible existing adjacent buildings. However, in the C2-2 overlay the Article III modifications apply. For a MIXED building (residential plus the C2-2 commercial use, 12-10 E3) ZR 35-01 applies the Chapter 5 bulk directly; for a RESIDENTIAL-ONLY building 34-11 applies Article II Chapter 3 bulk 'except as modified by ... 34-24', and 34-24(b)(1) 'shall' apply the Section 35-63 (inclusive) modifications for an R6-R12 equivalency, which 35-01's closing cross-reference sentence contemplates. Either pathway reaches 35-63, under which (E8) the street-wall location of a building 'shall be as set forth in Section 35-631'. R6B is not an R8-R12 Manhattan Core district, so 35-631(a) does not apply and 35-631(b) governs: at least 70 percent of the aggregate width of the street wall on EACH frontage must sit within 8 feet of that street line and extend to at least the minimum base height (30 ft for R6B) or the building height, whichever is less; up to 30 percent may recess beyond 8 feet, with recesses deeper than 10 ft on the wide frontage (Northern Boulevard) or 15 ft on the narrow frontage (215 Place) placed in an outer court. This supports repository backlog item DB-099, whose premise 'no Article III snapshot' is now outdated. The precise street-wall position within (b) stays conditional on whether the block has a prevailing street-wall frontage further from the street line (then the 23-431(a) line-up may be applied), and the 8-ft measure runs from the operative street line, which a mapped width does not fix. Q2 (setback). Both the residence-district chain (23-432 -> 23-433, E10/E11) and the overlay chain (35-632(a) -> 23-433, E12/E11) require a setback only for the portion of a building street wall that EXCEEDS the maximum base height (45 ft for R6B standard residences), provided between the minimum and maximum base heights. The benchmark three-storey 30 ft option equals the minimum base height and is well below the 45 ft maximum base height, so no setback is triggered. The street-width class (D-052: Northern Boulevard 100 ft = wide, 215 Place 60 ft = narrow) decides only the DEPTH of a setback that would apply above 45 ft (10 ft from a wide-street wall, 15 ft from a narrow-street wall); it is not triggered at or below the maximum base height. Q3 (side yards). Under 23-335 a side yard is NOT required for this building (23-335(b): all residences other than single/two-family detached), and the overlay 34-232 removes the requirement for any residential building; a side yard is permitted (optional), and any open area along a side lot line must be at least 5 feet wide. Only a single- or two-family detached residence would need two 5-ft side yards under 23-335(a), and even that is removed by 34-232 in the overlay. A side yard is not prohibited.

observed_facts: ZR 23-431(a): in R6B, R7B and R8B the street wall shall be located no closer/further from the street line than the closest/furthest street wall of an existing adjacent building on the same street frontage; where there is no prevailing street wall frontage, paragraph (b) may be applied.
ZR 23-431(b): along wide streets at least 70% of the aggregate width of street walls within 8 ft of the street line; along narrow streets within 10 ft.
ZR 34-11: in C1-C6, the bulk regulations of Article II Chapter 3 apply to all residential buildings except as modified by Sections 34-21 through 34-24.
ZR 34-24(b)(1): in Commercial Districts with an R6-R12 equivalency, 'the modifications to residential height and setback regulations set forth in Section 35-63, inclusive, shall be applied'.
ZR 35-01: the bulk regulations of Article III Chapter 5 apply to any mixed building in a Commercial District, and also apply where incorporated by cross-reference in other provisions.
ZR 35-63: for a Commercial District with an R6-R12 equivalency, the street-wall location of a building shall be as set forth in 35-631 and the height and setback provisions as set forth in 35-632.

ZR 35-631(a): the line-up rules apply only to an R8-R12 equivalency in the Manhattan Core. 35-631(b): for all buildings not subject to (a), at least 70% of the aggregate width of street walls within 8 ft of the street line, extending to at least the minimum base height or the building height whichever is less.

ZR 23-432 table (R6B row): minimum base height 30 ft; standard residences maximum base height 45 ft and maximum building height 55 ft. The section: a setback is provided 'for portions of a building street wall that exceed the maximum base height'.

ZR 23-433: at a height not lower than the minimum base height or higher than the maximum base height, a setback at least 10 ft deep from a street wall on a wide street, or 15 ft from a street wall on a narrow street; optional beyond 50 ft of a street line or at a 65-degree-or-less orientation.

ZR 35-632(a): heights come from the 23-432 table for the applicable Residence District, and a setback is provided for portions of a building street wall that exceed the maximum base height, per 23-433.
ZR 23-335: (a) single/two-family detached residences require two 5-ft side yards; (b) all other residences require no side yard, but any open area along a side lot line must be at least 5 ft wide.
ZR 34-232: in C1-C6 no side yard is required for any residential building; any open area along a side lot line must be at least 5 ft wide.

DCM Street Center Line at the lot envelope (6 features returned; selection of this lot's frontages): Northern Boulevard Streetwidth '100'; 215 Place Streetwidth '60'. (215 Street Streetwidth '60' and 45 Road '50' also returned by the envelope query but are not frontages of this corner lot; the list is not exhaustive.)
conclusion.interpretation: DRAFT reading awaiting independent review: (Q1) the C2-2 overlay makes 35-631(b) the governing street-wall rule for both a residential-only building (via 34-11 + 34-24(b)(1) + 35-63) and a mixed building (via 35-01 + 35-63) on this R6B corner lot, requiring at least 70% of each frontage's street wall within 8 ft of the street line; the exact position within (b) is conditional on the block's prevailing street-wall frontage and on the operative street-line position. (Q2) no setback is required for a building at or below the R6B maximum base height of 45 ft, so the benchmark three-storey 30 ft option needs none; the wide/narrow class sets only the depth of a setback that would apply above 45 ft. (Q3) no side yard is required (23-335(b); 34-232 in the overlay); one is optional with a 5-ft minimum if provided. Not a DOB determination.
conditions: Whether the 35-631(b) percentage rule governs the exact street-wall position, or its closing clause instead permits the 23-431(a) line-up, depends on whether either frontage of the block has a #prevailing street wall frontage# located further from the street line than 8 ft. 'Prevailing street wall frontage' is the ZR 12-10 defined term (E16): within 150 ft of the subject building's street wall, at least half of the aggregate width of street walls on the same side of the block are within two feet of their average distance from the street line (aggregate not less than 100 ft; the street wall is eligible when more than 50 percent of the segments are within two feet of that average). This is an unresearched adjacency fact. (The separate 15 ft / 25 ft / over-35-ft test is the 23-431(a) eligible-adjacent-building test, not the definition of a prevailing street wall frontage; 35-631(a) itself does not apply to this R6B Queens site.)

The 8-ft street-wall measure and any setback depth run from the operative street line; a DCM mapped width does not fix the street-line position (handoff: widths alone do not fix street-line positions). The street line comes from a survey or the approved plan.

The wide/narrow classification (Northern Boulevard 100 ft = wide; 215 Place 60 ft = narrow) rests on the DCM mapped widths and the owner-approved D-052 policy. The verbatim ZR 12-10 'street, wide' and 'street, narrow' definitions are now captured (E17, E18) and confirm that threshold (narrow below 75 feet, wide at or above 75 feet); the mapped width is still not a survey and does not fix the operative street-line position.
Whether the building is residential-only or mixed changes the applicability pathway (34-11/34-24(b)(1)/35-63 versus 35-01); both reach 35-631(b) here.
The setback depth (10 ft wide / 15 ft narrow) is relevant only for a portion of a building street wall above the 45 ft maximum base height; the benchmark 30 ft option does not reach it.
settled_by: an independent G1 review of the 34-11 -> 34-24(b)(1) -> 35-63 -> 35-631(b) cross-reference chain and the residential-only vs mixed-building reading
an adjacency survey of existing street walls on each frontage (to choose 35-631(a) vs (b))
the approved plan or a certified survey for the operative street-line positions

regression_cases: A building rising above the 45 ft maximum base height in R6B: a setback is required between 30 and 45 ft, at least 10 ft deep from the Northern Boulevard (wide) street wall and 15 ft from the 215 Place (narrow) street wall, per 23-433 / 35-632(a).
A single- or two-family detached residence: two 5-ft side yards under 23-335(a) in plain R6B, but none under 34-232 in the C2-2 overlay.
A block frontage with a prevailing street-wall frontage further from the street line than 8 ft: the 23-431(a) line-up may be applied instead of 35-631(b).
A residential-only building versus a mixed building: both reach 35-631(b) here (via 34-11/34-24(b)(1)/35-63 and via 35-01, respectively).
A street wall or wall beyond 50 ft of a street line, or oriented at 65 degrees or less to it: the 23-433 setback is optional (23-433(c)).
